premise: I poured my $125,000 widow’s inheritance into buying and restoring a historic Victorian turreted house with my daughter, who notarized a 50% ownership and a lifetime promise that I could live in the turret room surrounded by my late husband’s book collection; after a boutique hotel chain offered $830,000 for the property, she forged a quitclaim deed, sold the house, and slipped me a $5,000 “moving” check—I discovered the original agreement folded inside a hollowed‑out book in the turret, voided the sale, and now run “Turret of Betrayal Bed & Breakfast,” where she irons linens in a housekeeping dress that says “Pressed Out My Trust” and every guest receipt prints the deed‑fraud docket number.
